summary.text: A 77-year-old man with coronary artery disease, who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention in November 2017 and October 2019, had severe aortic stenosis with a mean trans-aortic valve pressure gradient of 47 mmHg. He received a 29 mm Edwards Sapien 3 valve by TAVR in November 2019; a day later the mean gradient was 15 mmHg, dyspnea improved and exercise tolerance was good.

One year later (October 2020) he developed worsening heart failure with pulmonary edema. ECG showed new-onset atrial fibrillation, and echocardiography showed an increased mean valve gradient of 48 mmHg, worsening mitral regurgitation and pulmonary hypertension. Response to intravenous inotropics and diuretics was poor, MDCT revealed HALT and RLM, and the authors diagnosed clinical leaflet thrombosis of the valve.

Rivaroxaban, a non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulant, was added to the concurrent single antiplatelet medication for the new-onset atrial fibrillation and leaflet thrombosis. Follow-up echocardiograms showed the gradient falling to 17 mmHg with reduced mitral regurgitation and pulmonary hypertension, and the authors reported satisfactory recovery with resolution of HALT and RLM on MDCT. Heart failure symptoms improved gradually but atrial fibrillation persisted.

In the fifth month after concomitant clopidogrel and rivaroxaban use he had a passage of tarry stool and a hemoglobin drop to 7.2 mg/dl. Upper gastrointestinal bleeding was treated with therapeutic endoscopy, proton pump inhibitors and blood transfusion. Clopidogrel was discontinued while rivaroxaban continued, and he was free from heart failure symptoms and bleeding events thereafter.
